units.scenario: B is Emma, Nam's Canadian friend, whom Nam meets on campus in the morning and again later in the day. Nam must greet her for the time of day, ask how she is, thank her and apologize, ask her to repeat something she didn't catch (Pardon?), and say goodbye with a good wish.

B is Mr. Brown running a short pronunciation check. He says one word from a pair (think/sink, ship/sheep, tell/ten, bed/bet); Nam must say which word she heard and repeat both words clearly, including the final sounds.

B is an exchange student at a university welcome party. Nam must say her first name, last name and nickname, where she is from and where she lives, that she is a student, ask him the same questions, and ask him to speak slowly when she does not understand.
B is a staff member at a university club sign-up table. Nam must say how many people are in her group, give her phone number digit by digit, and say her age and her younger sister's age.

B is Emma looking at family photos on Nam's phone. Nam must say who each person is (her parents, her younger sister Fah, her grandparents, an aunt and her husband and children), and ask about Emma's family.

B is a server at a Thai restaurant where Nam is having dinner with Emma. Nam must order food and drinks, say what she does or doesn't eat (I don't eat beef), ask for a spoon and fork, say she is full, and ask for the check.

B is Mr. Brown, who is making the class list for a new English course. Nam must spell her first name and last name letter by letter, check letters that sound alike (B or V? G or J? M or N?), and ask how to spell the names of new classmates.

B is Emma after class, when their things are mixed up on a café table. Nam must ask what things are, say which things are hers or Emma's (my / your), find her phone (in, on, under), and say something nice about Emma's new things.

B is Mr. Brown in Nam's English class. Nam must follow simple classroom instructions, say what she needs (a pen, a ruler), ask what a word means or how to say a Thai word in English, and say when she doesn't know.

B is a student at an international students' party at Nam's university, with guests from Japan, Korea, Vietnam and other countries. Nam must ask where people are from, say their nationality, and ask which languages they speak.

B is Emma, who is going to meet Nam's cousin at the airport but has never seen him. Nam must describe him simply (a tall man, short dark hair, young, handsome) and answer Emma's questions about how he looks.

B is Emma at a fruit stall in a Bangkok market; she has never tried many Thai fruits. Nam must name the fruits, say which ones she loves or doesn't like and how they taste, and ask Emma about her favorite fruit and sweets.
B is Emma at a pet café in Bangkok. Nam must say which animals she likes, say whether she has a pet, and describe it simply (its name, age, color, big or small, cute).
B is Emma on a free afternoon. Nam must say what music, movies, games and sports she likes, give a short opinion (fun, interesting, so-so), and suggest doing something together.

B is Emma shopping for a used bike and other things at a weekend market. Nam must describe the things they see (good or bad, clean or dirty, fast or slow, the same or different, real or not) and give her opinion with I think.

B is a friendly taxi driver chatting with Nam on the way home. Nam must say that she is a student and her parents are teachers, ask what the driver does and what his family members do, and ask where they work.
B is Emma planning to meet Nam for a movie. Nam must say what day and date it is, tell the time with half past, quarter past / to and a.m. / p.m., and agree on a day, a date and a time.
B is a shop assistant at a clothes shop in a Bangkok mall. Nam must ask about prices and colors, ask to try something on, understand prices in the thousands, and pay by card.

B is a passer-by near a BTS station. Nam must ask where places are (the post office, a pharmacy, a temple), understand directions with streets, blocks and traffic lights, and repeat them back to check.

B is Emma, who is writing about Thai students' days for a class project. Nam must describe her routine from waking up to going to bed, say how often she does things, and describe her sister Fah's school day (she gets up…, she doesn't…).
B is Emma calling from Canada during the holidays. Nam must describe the weather in Bangkok, ask about the weather in Canada, say how she feels and why, and ask how Emma feels.

B is a Bangkok taxi driver (and later a ticket seller at a boat pier). Nam must say where she is going, ask the driver to use the meter, mention the traffic jam, ask how much and how long it is, and say where to get off.

B is Emma visiting Nam's family house in Bangkok for the first time. Nam must welcome her in, show her the rooms, say what there is in each room and where things are, and answer when Emma asks to use the bathroom.

B is Emma on a video call from a park by the sea. Nam must ask what Emma and the people around her are doing, say what she is doing right now, and talk about what she can and can't do (swim, drive, ride a bike).

B is Emma calling Nam to meet up while Nam is on a noisy bus. Nam must answer the phone, say who she is, deal with a bad line (Can you hear me?), say that she is on her way, and arrange to call back later.

B is a barista at a café near the university. Nam must order drinks and a snack for herself and Emma, choose the size, hot or iced and less sugar, say for here or to go, and pay in cash or by QR code.

B is a cashier at a convenience store in Bangkok; Emma is with Nam. Nam must find snacks, drinks and toiletries, ask if they have something, say how many she wants, and answer the cashier (a bag? heat it up?).
B is a security guard at a temple and later at a swimming pool. Emma does not understand the signs; Nam must read them, explain what people can and can't do there, and ask the guard simple questions.

B is a police officer at a police box near a busy market. Nam is helping Emma, who is lost and can't find her bag. Nam must ask for help, explain the problem simply, describe the bag (color, what is in it) and thank the officer.

B is Emma; on Friday after class they meet at a big mall in Bangkok. Nam must agree on a time and a meeting place, find the food court and the movie theater (which floor? the escalator?), find seats, buy two movie tickets and check what time the mall closes.

B is a receptionist at a language school in Bangkok signing Nam up for an evening English course. Nam must give her full name, date and place of birth, nationality, address and email (spelling where needed), and check that the details are correct.

B is a new exchange student from Japan who has just arrived at Nam's university. Nam must say what and where she studies and what year she is in, show him important places on campus (the cafeteria, the bookstore, the computer lab), and tell him about a normal day at university.
B is a senior student at a university club fair. Nam must talk about the hobbies she enjoys, say what she can and can't do, and choose a club to join.
B is a doctor at the university clinic. Nam must describe her symptoms, answer the doctor's questions, and understand the advice about rest and medicine.
B is Mr. Brown, Nam's English teacher. Nam must explain her weekly timetable and her part-time job, say what she has to do, and ask what she doesn't have to do for the course.
B is Emma, a Canadian exchange student in Bangkok, before a long holiday weekend. Nam must find out Emma's plans, say what they are going to do together, and promise to help her.
B is Emma, who has just come back from a trip to the south of Thailand. Nam must ask what Emma did and tell her about her own weekend using the past simple.
B is Emma, who can't decide where to go on her next trip in Thailand. Nam must compare Bangkok, Chiang Mai and Phuket and recommend the best place for her.
B is Emma, who is going to Chiang Mai in December and asks about the weather. Nam must explain the Thai seasons, talk about the forecast, and say what Emma should pack.
B is a shop assistant in a clothes store at a Bangkok mall. Nam must find the right size and color, try something on, and describe the friend she is buying a present for.
B is a landlord showing Nam a room near her university. Nam must ask about the rent, the furniture and the rules, and decide whether to take the room.
B is a clerk at a bank in a shopping mall. Nam must open an account, ask about the ATM card, and find out how to send money to a friend in Canada.
B is a fitness trainer at the university gym. Nam must talk about the sports she plays, say how well she can do them, and agree on a weekly exercise plan.
B is Emma, who wants to know about Thai festivals. Nam must explain what people do at Songkran and Loy Krathong, ask how Canadians celebrate Christmas, and say which festival Emma should see.
B is Emma, who invites Nam to a birthday party. Nam must accept or politely refuse invitations, suggest another day, and agree on a time and place to meet.
B is Emma, who wants to learn to cook a Thai dish. Nam must say which ingredients they need, how much of each to buy, and explain the steps of the recipe.
B is an assistant in a mobile phone shop. Nam's phone is not working well; she must explain the problem, ask about a new charger, and ask how to set up her apps.
B is Mr. Brown, who asks his students about jobs. Nam must describe what different people do and where they work, and say what job she would like in the future and why.

B is Emma, who is making a list of places to visit before she goes home to Canada. Nam must ask where Emma has been, talk about her own travel experiences, and recommend a place Emma has never visited.
B is an airline employee at the baggage desk at Suvarnabhumi Airport. Nam's bag did not arrive; she must explain what happened, describe her bag, and ask what she should do next.
B is a receptionist at a small hotel in Chiang Mai. Nam must check in, ask about breakfast and the hotel's services, and politely complain that the air conditioning in her room isn't working.
B is Nam's manager during her summer internship at an office in Bangkok. Nam must find out what he wants her to do, agree on deadlines, and write a short polite email to a client.
B is Emma, Nam's new roommate. Nam must agree with her who does which chores, ask Emma to help with some jobs, and offer to do others herself.
B is an assistant at the customer service desk of a department store. Nam must explain what is wrong with something she bought, show her receipt, and ask for an exchange or a refund.
B is Mr. Brown, who is writing about childhood in Thailand and Canada. Nam must describe what she used to do as a child, say what has changed, and ask about Mr. Brown's childhood.
B is Emma, who wants to know about Nam's friends and family. Nam must describe people's personalities, using who / that / which, and say what kind of people she likes.
B is a man from abroad who has just moved to Bangkok. Nam must describe the neighborhood where she grew up, say how long she has lived there, and explain how Bangkok has changed.
B is a health coach at a campus health fair. Nam must describe her eating and sleeping habits, understand what will happen if she changes them, and agree on two new healthy habits.
B is Emma, who wants to watch something tonight. Nam must talk about the films, series and music she likes, explain what a film is about, and agree with Emma on what to watch.
B is a park ranger at Khao Yai National Park. Nam must ask which animals live in the park, understand the safety rules, and describe what she saw on the trail.
B is an emergency operator. Nam has just seen a motorcycle accident; she must say where she is, describe what happened and how the injured man is, and follow the operator's instructions.
B is a salesman in an electronics store. Nam wants a laptop for university; she must explain what she will use it for, compare two models, and decide which one to buy.
B is a waiter at a restaurant in Bangkok. Nam is having dinner with Emma; she must book a table, ask for recommendations, order for two people, and sort out a mistake on the check.
B is Mr. Brown, who meets Nam to talk about her progress. Nam must say how long she has been studying English, describe what is difficult for her, and ask for advice on how to improve.
B is a reporter from the campus radio station. Nam must explain an environmental problem in Bangkok, say what is being done about it, and suggest what students can do to help.
B is Mr. Brown, who asks the class to discuss the week's news. Nam must report a story she has read, say what people said about it, and give her opinion about whether the source is reliable.
B is an adviser at a study-abroad fair. Nam must explain what she has been studying, ask about entry requirements and scholarships, and say what she wants to study next.

B is Emma, who has been invited to dinner at a Thai family's home and is worried about doing something wrong. Nam must explain what Emma is supposed to do, what is considered rude, and how Thai and Canadian customs differ.
B is Emma, who wants to know how Nam manages her money. Nam must describe how she spends and saves, talk about what they would do if they had more money, and give advice about borrowing and lending.
B is Emma, who has had an argument with her boyfriend. Nam must listen, ask what happened, and give advice, using phrasal verbs about relationships.

B is Mr. Brown, who is preparing a class quiz about inventions. Nam must say who invented some everyday things, when they were invented and how they work, and argue which invention is the most important.
B is an officer at a tourist police station. Nam is helping a tourist whose bag has been stolen; she must explain what had happened, describe the thief, and ask what they should do next.

B is a researcher who is interviewing students about social media. Nam must describe her online habits, report what her friends post and say, and give her opinion about the good and bad sides of social media.
B is a tourist from Australia staying at a guesthouse in Bangkok. Nam must recommend places to visit, explain what each place is known for, and help him plan a one-week route around Thailand.

B is Mr. Brown, who asks students to present the life of a famous person. Nam must tell the life story of someone she admires, say what that person had done before becoming famous, and answer questions about them.

B is Emma, who is in a thoughtful mood before she goes back to Canada. Nam must talk about what she wishes were different in her life, her dreams for the future, and what she would do in some imaginary situations.
B is a market researcher doing a survey in a shopping mall. Nam must describe how and where she shops, say which ads persuade her to buy things, and compare shopping online with shopping in stores.
B is the coordinator of a volunteer project that teaches English at a rural school. Nam must explain why she wants to volunteer, say what she has been doing, and offer to help with different tasks.
B is Mr. Brown, who leads a class discussion about life in 2050. Nam must make predictions about technology, work and cities, say how sure she is, and talk about a plan that has changed.
B is Emma, who has been hearing strange noises in her apartment at night. Nam must suggest possible explanations, say what must or can't be true, and talk about famous unexplained mysteries.

B is an HR manager interviewing Nam for a graduate trainee position at an international company. Nam must describe her education, skills and experience, explain why she wants the job, and ask questions about the position.

B is a customer relations manager at an online travel company. The hotel Nam booked was not as described; she must explain the problem formally, refer to her booking details, and ask for compensation.
B is Mr. Brown, who chairs a class debate: "Should university education be free?" Nam must give her opinion, support it with reasons, respond politely to the other side, and sum up her position.
B is Emma, who asks Nam to tell her about the most embarrassing day of her life. Nam must tell the story in order, set the scene, build up to the key moment, and answer Emma's questions.

B is a student adviser at a university in Toronto, where Nam has just started an exchange semester. Nam must compare life in Thailand and Canada, describe what she is getting used to, and ask for advice about the things she finds difficult.
B is a guide at an art gallery in Bangkok. Nam must describe the paintings and photographs she likes, say how they make her feel, and discuss whether creativity can be taught.
B is a colleague who notices that Nam looks exhausted. Nam must describe what is causing her stress, say what she would rather her manager did, and agree on practical ways to switch off after work.

B is Emma, who has just made a big mistake at work. Nam must ask what happened, say what Emma should or shouldn't have done, talk about a mistake of her own, and help Emma see what she can learn from it.
B is a law student who leads a discussion group. Nam must explain some Thai laws and rules, say which ones she agrees or disagrees with, and talk about people's rights at work and online.
B is a possible investor at a student start-up competition. Nam must present her idea for a small business, describe the market and sales trends, and answer questions about costs and risks.

B is Mr. Brown, who watches Nam rehearse a five-minute presentation about her research project. Nam must introduce her topic, guide the audience through her slides and data, sum up, and handle questions.

B is a customer service agent for an internet company. Nam's home internet has been down for two days; she must explain the problem on the phone, follow the agent's instructions, and arrange a visit from a technician.

B is a student from another country at a Model United Nations meeting. Nam must explain a global problem, describe whether it is getting better or worse, and propose what countries should do about it.
B is a career coach. Nam must describe her long-term goals, explain what she has already done to reach them, say what success means to her, and agree on her next steps.
B is Nam's landlord, who wants to raise the rent on her apartment. Nam must negotiate: compare her options, make offers with conditions, find a compromise, and reach an agreement.

B is a guest at an international networking event in Bangkok. Nam must start a conversation with a stranger, keep it going by showing interest, exchange contact details, and end the conversation politely.
